about.text: Yogurt, also spelled yoghurt, is a food produced by bacterial fermentation of milk. The bacteria ferment the sugars in the milk and produce lactic acid, which acts on milk protein to give yogurt its texture and characteristic tart flavor. Yogurt is most commonly made from cow's milk, but milk from water buffalo, goats, ewes, mares, camels, and yaks can also be used.

how.text: The two bacteria help each other, so together they acidify faster and make far more acetaldehyde, yoghurt's key flavour, than either does alone. Heating the milk first denatures 70–80 % of the whey protein, which binds to the casein, so the acid sets the milk into a firm gel that holds its whey.
